nodes.description: In zebrafish embryos, mRNA encoding the mutant PACS1 induces craniofacial cartilage defects, most likely in a dominant-negative fashion, through aberrant specification and migration of SOX10-positive cranial neural crest cells, while enteric neural crest is spared. In transfected cells the mutant protein forms cytoplasmic aggregates with increased stability. This is the proposed basis of the facial gestalt. The model is overexpression of human mRNA in fish, and the result predates the HDAC6 mechanism; how the two connect has not been tested.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, consistent with the human pathology, expression of mutant PACS1 mRNA in zebrafish embryos induces craniofacial defects most likely in a dominant-negative fashion. This phenotype is driven by aberrant specification and migration of SOX10-positive cranial, but not enteric, neural-crest cells.

nodes.description: Mature PACS1(+/R203W) glutamatergic neurons and cortical organoids differentiated from isogenic stem cells show reduced expression of synaptic signaling genes and prolonged network bursts with longer interspike intervals on multielectrode arrays and calcium imaging. Neural precursors show few changes, so the deficit appears with neuronal maturation. Organoid proteomics converge on the same developmental processes and on known neurodevelopmental disorder and autism risk genes. This node is the proposed substrate for intellectual disability, autism and seizures; no study has yet connected a specific circuit change to a specific clinical feature.

nodes.description: In PACS1 syndrome mice, prefrontal cortical neurons carry more elaborate dendrites that are beaded with varicosities and have fewer spines and fewer functional synapses. nodes.description: PACS1 binds cytoplasmic dynein-1 heavy chain and is needed to keep furin at the trans-Golgi network. The PACS1 Arg203Trp-HDAC6 complex recruits the dynein adaptor BICD2, and the result is a dynein loss-of-function phenotype: cargo motility assays show reduced dynein initiation frequency and velocity, which HDAC6 inhibition or the dynein regulator Lis1 rescues. This places the syndrome among microtubule trafficking disorders.

evidence.reference_title: PACS1 syndrome mutation disrupts dynein-mediated cargo transport via HDAC6 and BICD2.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that PACS1R203W-HDAC6 recruits the adaptor BICD2, forming a complex that disperses the Golgi and impairs dynein function. Cargo motility assays revealed that PACS1R203W reduces dynein initiation frequency and velocity, defects rescued by HDAC6 inhibition or by expressing the dynein regulator Lis1.

nodes.description: PACS1 binds the catalytic domains of the class IIb deacetylase HDAC6 through its FBR. Arg203Trp increases this interaction and aberrantly potentiates HDAC6 activity, lowering acetylation of its substrates alpha-tubulin and cortactin in patient-derived neural progenitor cells and mouse neurons.

evidence.snippet: PACS1-related disorder (PACS1-RD), also known as Schuurs-Hoeijmakers syndrome, is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder predominantly caused by the recurrent de novo c.607 C > T p.(Arg203Trp) gain-of-function variant.

nodes.description: The recurrent c.607C>T p.(Arg203Trp) substitution, and the rarer p.(Arg203Gln) at the same residue, lie in the furin-binding region (FBR, residues 101-273) of PACS1. NMR of the FBR shows that a central unstructured segment of PACS1 folds back across the FBR and contacts a positively charged loop that contains Arg203; this intramolecular contact restrains the PACS1-HDAC6 interaction, and the tryptophan substitution disrupts it. The allele is therefore a gain of function. Consistent with this, a three-generation family heterozygous for a deletion of PACS1 exons 12-24 lacked the facial gestalt, intellectual disability and brain anomalies of the syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: The R203W substitution drives PACS-1 syndrome by disrupting intramolecular regulation.
evidence.snippet: We present the solution structure of a chimeric PACS-1 FBR and use NMR to demonstrate that the PACS-1/HDAC6 interaction is regulated by an intramolecular mechanism involving the central unstructured region of PACS-1 folding back across the FBR and engaging in contacts with an extended, positively charged loop. The R203W substitution, located in this loop, disrupts this regulatory interaction

evidence.snippet: This pathogenic mutation lies on a solvent-exposed surface of the FBR and does not disrupt complex formation. Instead, Pacs1-R203W remains dependent on Wdr37 for stability and its levels can be reduced through targeted Wdr37 proteolytic degradation.

nodes.description: Mice expressing PACS1 R203W reproduce the neuronal Golgi, dendrite, spine and synaptic phenotypes, which antisense depletion of Hdac6 or PACS1 rescues. A standard germline Pacs1 R201W knock-in was embryonic lethal, so expression was restricted to forebrain neurons. Craniofacial and systemic features were not the subject of the study.

A Pacs1-specific 2'-O-methoxyethyl gapmer antisense oligonucleotide given intracerebroventricularly to newborn Pacs1 R201W/+ mice (R201W is the mouse equivalent of human R203W) depleted PACS1 and rescued excitatory synaptic transmission. Pacs1 loss itself did not disturb synapses in the same study, which is the rationale for lowering PACS1 in patients. Not tested in patients.
